unsettled: The annex of RA 9165 was not read. Sec. 3(h) and 3(j) define precursors and dangerous drugs by the UN Convention tables and schedules "as enumerated in the attached annex", but no official copy with the annex could be read: the DDB copy of the Act ends in Section 84 without the annex; the Official Gazette and Senate issuances-library pages could not be fetched; the Senate PDFs found were bills; the DTI trade-repository copy ends in Section 92. The DDB's consolidated list (as of 20 July 2026) was used as the current official list.

Ten DDB regulations are scanned PDFs with no readable text, among them Board Regulation No. 1, s. 2020 (immediate adoption of changes in the scope of control under the three UN conventions) and the GBL, CBD, plants, esketamine, flubromazolam, acetylfentanyl, alpha-PVP, 3-CMC and MDMB-4en-PINACA regulations. For these, only titles were read (twice). An OCR or text copy would let their conditions be checked.

Not-found items and UN control. Every not-found row is absent from the DDB list (two readings). But Board Regulation No. 1, s. 2014, Sec. 3(1)(a)(i) obliges the DDB to issue an implementing regulation automatically for UN scheduling decisions, and Board Regulation No. 1, s. 2020 (unreadable) adopts changes in the UN scope of control immediately. If the site's UN treaty layer shows any not-found item (e.g. a 2C-x, NEP, 2-MMC, 4-BMC) under the 1961 or 1971 Convention, the editor must decide whether it is a Philippine dangerous drug although the DDB list does not print it.

Philippine Schedules 1-5. Annex A of Board Regulation No. 1, s. 2014 gives the criteria of Philippine Schedules 1-5 and aligns them with Convention schedules, but its table text is flattened. As read (three readings): Schedule 1 row: 1961 Schedule IV and 1971 Schedule I; Schedule 2 row: labels "Schedule I Schedule II Schedule II"; Schedule 3: 1971 Schedule III; Schedule 4: 1961 Schedule III and 1971 Schedule IV; Schedule 5: Philippine-only dangerous drugs. Because the column of each label is uncertain, no Philippine schedule number is given for Convention-listed items. Section 93 substances are put in Philippine Schedule 5 by Sec. 2(2) of that regulation (stated in the ketamine, GBL and Salvia rows).

MDMB-4en-PINACA: the DDB list prints it in the 1971 Schedule II list ("MDMB-4enPINACA (New 2021)"), while the index title of 2025 Board Regulation No. 13 reads "Inclusion of MDMB-4en-PINACA in Schedule I of the 1971 UN Convention on Psychotropic Substances" (both read twice; the regulation itself is unreadable). It is recorded as Schedule II per the list.

Cannabidiol (CBD): the list names only "Drug Products Containing Cannabidiol (CBD) with no more than 0.1 percent Tetrahydrocannabinol", placed in Philippine Schedule 4 (Board Regulation No. 3, s. 2020, unreadable). Whether CBD in other forms is controlled is not stated: plant-derived extracts fall under the cannabis definition of RA 9165 Sec. 3(v) and the 1961 Schedule 1 entry "CANNABIS AND CANNABIS RESIN, EXTRACTS and TINCTURES"; synthetic CBD is not addressed. Its medical_use is taken from the Annex A criteria of Philippine Schedule 4.

Esketamine: named only under "Board issuances" (Board Regulation No. 5, s. 2021, a prescription rule for the nasal spray), not under "DDB Regulations". Its control rests on ketamine's regulation (DDB Regulation No. 3, s. 2005, Sec. 1: ketamine "including its salts, isomers, and salts of isomers"). Recorded as listed; please confirm.

Salvinorin A: not named. Board Regulation No. 3, s. 2015 classifies Salvia divinorum and "its resin, extract, tincture or other forms"; whether isolated or synthetic salvinorin A is covered is for the editor. Row kept draft.

Ketamine's prescription exception (DDB Regulation No. 3, s. 2005, Sec. 2: prescribed preparations within vial and dose limits are excepted from Sec. 1) is recorded as medical_use. Whether later regulations (Board Regulation No. 1, s. 2014, which comprehensively amended Board Regulation No. 3, s. 2003; Board Regulation No. 10, s. 2025 and No. 5, s. 2026 on ordinary prescriptions) changed it was not checked.

medical_use for Salvia divinorum and GBL is left null. Under Sec. 2(2) of Board Regulation No. 1, s. 2014 they are Philippine Schedule 5, whose Annex A criteria begin "has a currently accepted medical use in treatment in the Philippines"; applying that wording to these two substances is for the editor.

"If named" plant items (ayahuasca; peyote or San Pedro): not named in any list read, so no rows. Board Regulation No. 3, s. 2019 classifies as dangerous drugs plants containing substances listed in the 1961 or 1971 Conventions or classified by the DDB, "or are sources thereof" (title, read twice). Such a clause may reach DMT- or mescaline-containing plants, but the regulation's text (scanned) could not be read to see whether it names any plant.

Section 93 of RA 9165 was not read in an official copy of the Act; its content is taken from Board Regulation No. 1, s. 2014, Sec. 3(1)(a) and the preamble of Board Regulation No. 3, s. 2015 (both read twice).

Currency of the list: the DDB list (as of 20 July 2026) does not print the substances added by Board Regulations Nos. 2, 3 and 4, s. 2026 (N-desethyl etonitazene, N-pyrrolidino isotonitazene, MDMB-FUBINACA), which the index lists, so later regulations can precede the list. No title in the index (2002 to 2026 No. 5) names any not-found item; the index may be re-checked before publication.
